newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end firm after touching 3-month high.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end firm after touching 3-month high.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended firmer on Monday after touching three-month highs on follow through from Friday's bullish USDA crop data and on concerns heat in key South American growing regions would damage crops.
The January contract peaked at $7.38 per bushel early Monday, topping the high of $7.37 set on October 11.
"There's not much relief in sight in southern Brazil and the stocks are tight, the tightest stocks-to-usage ratio in about 20 years," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Brazilian growers said some areas in Rio Grande do Sul remained without rain and were starting to suffer losses.

USDA on Friday pegged 1996 U.S. soybean output at 2.382 billion bushels, below average expectations for 2.407 billion. USDA said the 1996-97 U.S. soybean carryover would total 155 million bushels, below the previous forecast for 180 million.
However, gains in soybeans were limited by increased farmer selling in the cash market and reports that cash basis levels continued to slide.
Soybeans closed 1-1/4 to 8-1/4 cents per bushel higher with March up 7-1/2 at $7.36-3/4.
Volume was said to be heavy with funds accounting for at least 15 million bushels in soybean purchases.
On the day, Chicago Corp bought nine million bushels March and Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch Futures each bought five million March, traders said.
Volume was estimated at 75,000 contracts, compared with Friday's volume of 91,363 contracts.
